projects.title: Walnut Cookie Slab Table Set
projects.description: Matched coffee and end table set built around walnut cookie slabs — cross-sections that preserve the full growth ring and live edge of the tree. The slabs required flattening with a custom-built router sled jig before the natural voids and cracks could be filled with epoxy. Welded steel bases were fabricated for both pieces, giving the organic slab tops a clean industrial counterpoint. The set lives together as a cohesive suite in the client's living room.

projects.title: Slab Mirror
projects.description: Wall mirror built from the same birds-eye maple slab used in the Arachno Coffee Table. The slab was ripped down the center along its natural live edge, and the mirror glass set between the two halves — the void between them becomes the mirror, mimicking the river table concept in a vertical format. A key structural challenge: mirror glass alone can't support the weight of the slabs, so a backer plate was fabricated and the mirror sandwiched between it and the wood, transferring the load through the frame rather than the glass. The result looks like a single continuous slab of wood floating around a mirror.

projects.title: Autonomous RC Boat
projects.description: Undergraduate mechatronics project: an RC boat converted into an autonomous obstacle-avoidance platform. The approach was self-derived — looking at the dev kit components available, the idea emerged to mount an ultrasonic sensor on a servo and sweep it across the field of view, building a spatial map of what's ahead. No AI, no LIDAR, no prior framework — just first-principles thinking that happened to reinvent phased-array radar logic from scratch. The boat uses that distance map to steer around obstacles in real time.

projects.title: Arachno Side Table
projects.description: Miniaturization of the Arachno Coffee Table concept into a side table format — same brazed steel rod lattice, scaled down and reworked as a tall pedestal. The lathe-turned wood feet carry over from the coffee table, turned from offcuts of the same slab material. After building the physical piece, the design language was extended in CAD to explore what a full furniture line could look like: a nightstand with a drawer and the arachno lattice as the base structure, and a dresser with the lattice as a plinth and the brazing detail translated into drawer pulls throughout. Neither has been built yet, but the renders show how the joinery technique scales to more complex, functional forms.

projects.title: Arachno Coffee Table
projects.description: Second-generation application of the brazed steel rod joinery technique developed in the Claro Walnut Coffee Table — this time constrained into a rectangular, grid-like base geometry. Where the original base was organic and radial, the Arachno base imposes order on the chaos: rods cut, bent, and brazed mid-air into a repeating structural lattice. Topped with a walnut slab and epoxy river pour. The feet are custom-turned on the lathe from offcuts of the same top slab, tying the wood and steel together as one cohesive piece.

projects.title: BeethoVAN — Modular Concert Stages
projects.description: Senior capstone project at SD Mines in partnership with the Rushmore Music Festival — a travelling orchestra that brings classical music to rural communities across the Northern Great Plains. The team designed and built the BeethoVAN: a fully outfitted cargo trailer serving as a mobile concert hall with indoor/outdoor performance capability, instrument storage, HVAC, solar power, and AV systems. My primary contribution was the modular aluminum stage system. No off-the-shelf stage had the combination of features required, so the stages were designed and built from scratch. Work included determining all structural loads, hand calculations for beam deflection using composite beam theory to account for the wood deck and aluminum frame acting together, and FEA to validate the results. The stages feature height-adjustable legs with cam lock handles fabricated from laminated sheet metal and modified McMaster components — built to be as cheap as possible while still locking securely under load. Also welded and assembled the articulating piano platform: an actuator-driven frame that stores the grand piano vertically during transport to minimize string detune from road vibration. The BeethoVAN began touring in summer 2023 and has been covered by SD Mines and the Rapid City Journal.

projects.title: Aircraft Rib Wrinkle Prediction
projects.description: Aerospace engineering internship project: predicting and mitigating wrinkle formation in hydroformed aluminum aircraft ribs. Ran forming simulations in Altair HyperForm to predict where wrinkles would initiate, then designed relief cutouts into the tooling to redistribute material flow before those regions collapsed. The physical result — a 3D-printed mandrel with the tuned relief cutouts and a formed aluminum rib — validated the simulation approach.

projects.title: Bobcat Manufacturing Engineering Co-op
projects.description: Manufacturing engineering co-op at Bobcat. Two main workstreams: prototype build support for the L35 small articulated loader, and weld line optimization for the snowblower attachment line. The L35 work was early-stage — the first production-intent prototype after the initial mule — with no formal tooling yet. Wrote the initial standard work instructions for the L35, documenting every part number, installation method, and torque specification. Worked closely with the design team to ensure the manufactured assembly matched design intent, and participated in FMEA sessions to identify and mitigate assembly failure modes. On the snowblower weld line, conducted time studies across stations, identified cycle time imbalances, and redistributed weld tasks to level the line flow. The L35 has since launched as Bobcat's most powerful small articulated loader.

projects.title: Clinic-in-a-Can Modular Walls
projects.description: Collaborative project designed during Innovation Studio 1 with Clinic-in-a-Can, a local nonprofit that deploys medical clinics in shipping containers to emergency situations globally. The goal was to create a modular wall system to link multiple shipping containers together, forming a reliable, weatherproof seal around the joined perimeter. This proposed solution features interlocking panels with insulated foam interiors sandwiched between a structural wood layer and a durable steel exterior. These segments chain together to secure the open gaps between containers. A scaled 3D-printed prototype was created to demonstrate the geometric interlocking joints, showcased here alongside preliminary concept sketches and the main CAD model.

projects.title: Side Table Home Garden
projects.description: A fully automatic indoor garden disguised as a side table, designed for my Innovation Studio 1 graduate course. The prompt was to make fresh produce more accessible to people in food deserts — rather than adding another appliance to the home, this integrates a garden into existing furniture. The prototype features a soil moisture sensor, grow lights, a peristaltic pump for automated watering, and a camera for machine vision plant monitoring, all connected to the web for remote access. The lid is height-adjustable for easy access to the garden. This was a rapid prototyping class focused on the thinking process over a polished final product.

projects.title: Brass Wire Joinery Tables
projects.description: 100% original design — my favorite pieces. Built the side table first, then loved the technique so much it expanded into a matching console table. Walnut round top on a steel and brass frame.
